subject: Candidate evaluation variance — mediation and offer timing
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Candidate evaluation variance — mediation and offer timing

Hi Neha and Monica,

Quick note on Evan Brooks (backend infra candidate, onsite 11/29). The panel scores are all over the place — two panelists rated him comfortably in band, one gave low technical scores because of perceived lacking experience with our runtime internals. The recruiter is pushing to make an offer tomorrow to avoid losing him; I want to avoid a rushed decision if there is a genuine calibration issue.

Can we do a short mediation: 1) review the scoring sheets and written notes, 2) ask the low-scoring interviewer for concrete examples of missed expectations, and 3) decide whether we can justify banding at L5 vs L4. If we escalate, I want HR/comp to hold the offer until we have committee signoff.

I've attached the panel scores and the candidate homework. Links to recordings are in the Drive folder below.

Request: Neha, can you lead the mediation and let me know if you need any extra materials? Monica, please confirm the candidate's current comp expectations and whether we have slack in the band to bridge a gap if needed.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Hiring Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Candidate evaluation variance — mediation and offer timing

Thanks Tessa — I can run the mediation today. Initial asks from me:

- Monica: please upload the raw score sheets and the candidate's homework (I only have the summary).
- Karthik: can you give a 3–4 bullet rationale for your low score so we can include it in the record? Concrete examples (question number, expected behavior, and actual answer) are most helpful.
- Tessa: confirm whether we are comfortable pausing any offer timeline until mediation concludes (I recommend yes).

I will:
- Convene a 30-min call with the three interviewers and recruiter this afternoon.
- Produce a short mediation note outlining whether the variance is due to rubric mismatch, interviewer strictness, or candidate gap.
- If we can't reach alignment, I'll escalate to Compensation Committee and attach the mediation note + artifacts.

Attach: sample mediation template (HR_mediation_template.docx).

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Talent Partner | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:15:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Candidate evaluation variance — mediation and offer timing

Thanks — quick context from my side: I interviewed Evan for systems design and a short runtime debugging exercise. My low score reflects two things:

1) Systems design: Evan's components were fine at a high level but lacked a concrete plan for cache invalidation and KV cache coherence. I marked that as a gap because our role requires ownership of multi-region cache correctness.
2) Debugging exercise: Evan struggled to explain the trade-offs of different attention caching strategies under long sequences; his solution would degrade memory usage in our worst-case workloads.

I'm happy to walk through the exact questions on the mediation call and point to the timestamps in the recording (see Drive link). I don't think this is interviewer strictness — the other two panelists leaned more on product fit and collaboration signals, not the low-level correctness I care about for this role.

If the team decides the role is more product/feature-first rather than deep runtime ownership, we could consider L4, but that should come with explicit adjustments to the role description.

—Karthik
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Candidate evaluation variance — mediation and offer timing

Following up with scheduling and comp context:

- Evan is currently interviewing with another company and has asked for a decision by Friday (12/04). He listed a target of $200–220k base with typical RSU expectations for our region.
- Our currently approved range for backend infra L5 is $195–215k base; L4 range is $165–185k. There is some headroom at the top of L5 but minimal.
- I uploaded the raw score sheets and the candidate homework to the Drive folder and attached the three interview notes as a PDF.

Proposed path:
- Do the 30-min mediation call today (Neha, 11:30am PT slot available).
- If mediation finds the concern is rubric mismatch, we can recalibrate and proceed with an L5 offer at the committee-approved midpoint.
- If mediation confirms technical gap, recommend offering L4 with explicit role outcomes and shorter review cycle (6 months) to re-evaluate.

I will draft a preliminary offer letter and hold it in DocuSign as 'pending' so we can sign and send within 24 hours of final decision if we want. Please confirm acceptance of the mediation plan.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Recruiter | Redwood Inference
Attachment: interview-notes-20261129.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Candidate evaluation variance — mediation and offer timing

Summary from mediation (call held 11:30am PT):

- Outcome: Partial calibration issue + substantive technical concern. Two panelists agree candidate is broadly strong; one panelist (Karthik) identified a role-critical gap in cache coherence and certain runtime trade-offs.
- Recommendation: Escalate to Compensation Committee for an exception if the hiring manager (Tessa) remains convinced of candidate upside and can articulate mitigation steps. Options: 
  a) Proceed with L5 offer at top-of-band with a documented 6-month technical milestone plan and manager discretion for acceleration.
  b) Offer L4 with accelerated review at 6 months and explicit milestones for L5 promotion; inform candidate transparently.
- Action items:
  1) Tessa: send a short written rationale (3–5 bullets) on why you prefer option (a) — highlight candidate signals that outweigh the gap and the mitigation plan.
  2) Monica: prepare provisional L5 offer sheet and L4 alternative, hold both in DocuSign.
  3) Neha/HR: I will file a formal comp-committee request and attach mediation notes + artifacts (Drive links and panel scores).

I will submit the comp packet by EOD today for committee review tomorrow. Please add any additional evidence to the Drive folder by 4pm PT.

-Neha
